interpretation_guardrail: Fewer groups is not automatically better. A grouping that merges neighboring words or unrelated strokes is a regression even when review count falls.

post_run_acting_safe_visual_review.decision: Promote balanced 5x15 grouping as an editable initial colour grouping, never as final word ownership. Preserve tight and broad as one-click split/merge challengers.
post_run_acting_safe_visual_review.difficulties: Tight grouping leaves detached dots, ascenders, and broken strokes as separate colours. Broad grouping visibly merges neighboring words, including `thoroughly enjoying`; balanced can still merge `forgetful brother` and retain isolated speck groups. Fewer groups alone is not quality.
post_run_acting_safe_visual_review.meaning: Balanced grouping reduced 36-168 raw eight-connected evidence components to 10-22 left-to-right colour groups (58.33%-92.26% reduction) while preserving every exact ink pixel. Across six boards, many groups visually align with whole words. This is a promising human-effort transformation even though split/merge correction remains necessary.
post_run_acting_safe_visual_review.visual_scope: All six generated source/tight/balanced/broad grouping boards only; no sealed human page, answer, mask, or evaluator board was opened.

selection_rule: Apply three frozen anisotropic grouping kernels to the six prior automatically selected cross-page lines. Group labels may change; the exact anchor-plus-proposal ink pixels may not.
